biblia.title: Biblia — Semitic Jew
biblia.subtitle: Explore the Tanakh, Apocrypha, New Testament, dietary laws, reference tools, extra-biblical sources, and Black history through Scripture, history, and logic.

note.label: Study Hub
note.h2: Scripture, history, law, and identity in one place.
note.p: This hub organizes the core reading tools and study resources for biblical literacy, Israelite identity, historical context, and disciplined research.

cards.title: The Tanakh
cards.desc: Law, historical writings, wisdom, prophets, and restoration hope organized for reading and study.

cards.title: The Apocrypha
cards.desc: Second Temple history, wisdom, resistance, restoration, and Israelite writings with chapter access.

cards.title: New Testament
cards.desc: The testimony of Christ, apostolic history, letters, and Revelation in Israelite context.

cards.title: Dietary Laws
cards.desc: Clean and unclean categories from the Law presented for practical study.

cards.title: Extra-Biblical Sources
cards.desc: Historical witnesses, regions, maps, and sources connected to the biblical world.

cards.title: Bible References
cards.desc: Reference tools for terms, themes, people, and Scripture-connected study.

cards.title: Israelite Encyclopedia
cards.desc: People, terms, ethnonyms, and source-linked entries for deeper research.

cards.title: Black History & Biblical Identity
cards.desc: Ancient Black presence, Israelite scattering, captivity, colonization, resistance, myths, and study paths.

tanakh.title: Tanakh — Semitic Jew
tanakh.description: Explore the Tanakh through the Law, historical writings, wisdom literature, prophets, and restoration texts in a structured Scripture reader.
tanakh.subtitle: Explore the Law, historical writings, wisdom literature, prophets, and visions of restoration in a structured canon layout.

guide.p: Torah foundations: creation, covenant, commandments, priesthood, and national order.

guide.h2: Acts of Israelites in the Land
guide.p: Israel’s judges, kings, exile, return, and covenant consequences in history.
Instruction, worship, suffering, prudence, fear of God, and righteous living.
Rebuke, repentance, judgment, restoration, and the hope of Israel.
Kingdom hope, prophetic visions, and the promised repair of Israel.

newtestament.title: New Testament — Semitic Jew
newtestament.description: Explore the New Testament through the testimony of Christ, apostolic history, letters, assemblies, Israelite context, and the vision of Revelation.
newtestament.subtitle: Explore the testimony of Christ, apostolic history, letters to Israel and the nations, and the vision of Revelation.

guide.p: The testimony of Christ through Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John.
Acts records the spread of the testimony, the apostles, and early assemblies.
Instruction, correction, order, faith, and doctrine across the assemblies.

guide.h2: Letters to the House of Israel
guide.p: Hebrews, James, Peter, John, and Jude address faithfulness, trial, and endurance.
Revelation gives judgment, kingdom hope, endurance, and final restoration.

apocrypha.title: Apocrypha — Semitic Jew
apocrypha.description: Explore the Apocrypha through historical narratives, wisdom writings, additions to Daniel and Esther, Maccabean history, Esdras, and prayer texts.
apocrypha.subtitle: Explore additional historical, wisdom, and restoration writings that preserve important context for Israel’s story.

guide.p: Stories of faithfulness, exile, deliverance, courage, and covenant memory.
Instruction, discipline, prayer, wisdom, and exhortation among Israel.
Supplemental accounts tied to exile, judgment, vindication, and deliverance.
Resistance, persecution, temple cleansing, law, identity, and national struggle.
Restoration themes, repentance, prophecy, grief, hope, and covenant repair.
